1G (Number Theory)

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 93
1G OurBigBook.com
A Carmichael number is a composite N such that aN−1≡1(modN) for every a coprime to N. For p∣N, choose by CRT a number whose residue mod p is a primitive root; its order p−1 divides N−1. If p2∣N, choose instead a primitive root modulo p2; then p(p−1)∣N−1, impossible because p∣N. Thus N is square-free. Write N=pm. Since p−1∣N−1, also p−1∣m−1; compositeness gives m>1, hence m≥p and p≤N​. This is Korselt criterion.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

3H (Coding & Cryptography)

Words: 72 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 72
3H OurBigBook.com
A Rabin cryptosystem chooses Blum primes p,q, publishes N=pq, and encrypts m as c=m2modN. Decryption takes square roots modulo p and q, combines them with CRT, and uses redundancy to select the intended one of four roots. Here 23552≡25(mod2773), while the obvious root is 5. Thus
gcd(2355−5,2773)=47,gcd(2355+5,2773)=59.
(2)
So 2773=47⋅59 is factored, allowing all future square roots and hence all ciphertexts to be decrypted.

6C (Mathematical Biology)

Words: 73 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 73
6C OurBigBook.com
Scaling by K, the positive fixed point is x=1. Linearization xt​=1+ϵt​ gives ϵt+1​=ϵt​−rϵt−1​, with characteristic polynomial λ2−λ+r. The Jury conditions put both roots inside the unit circle exactly for 0<r<1. At r=1 the roots are e±iπ/3, sixth roots of unity. The discrete Hopf resonance therefore creates a small period-six branch; expansion of the nonlinear recurrence on the centre eigenspace supplies the nonzero amplitude.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

Solution

Words: 114
7D OurBigBook.com
The identity theorem says analytic functions agreeing on a set with an interior accumulation point agree throughout a connected domain. Analytic continuation is an analytic function on a larger connected domain agreeing on a nonempty overlap. Factor the denominator as (t+i)(t−z). For ℑz<0, contour closure below gives
F(z)=−2πiz+ie−5iz−e−5​,
(4)
with a removable value at −i; this entire expression is the continuation. For ℑz>0, the displayed real-axis integral encloses only −i and equals 2πie−5/(z+i), so it is not that continuation. Finally 1/n→0 only at a boundary point of D, so the zeros do not determine G; for example G(z)=sin(π/z) is nonzero and has them all.

A form ax2+bxy+cy2 is positive definite when a>0 and d=b2−4ac<0; equivalence is change by SL2​(Z), and reduced means ∣b∣≤a≤c with the standard boundary sign convention. Translating x↦x+my reduces ∣b∣, and swapping variables reduces a; discriminant bounds force termination. For a reduced form, ∣b∣≤a≤∣d∣/3​ and b≡d(mod2). Discriminant −28 has one primitive reduced class, represented by x2+7y2. Therefore an odd prime is represented exactly when it splits in Q(−7​), namely (p/7)=1, with the ramified exception p=7. Thus p=7 or p≡1,9,11,15,23,25(mod28).
